full_text_en:
Rugao Printing Machinery Factory v. Yide Company — dispute over infringement of trademark exclusive right

[Ruling Summary]

Pursuant to paragraph (5) of Article 52 of the Trademark Law, the act of purchasing used equipment manufactured by others, refurbishing it, removing the original trademark identifiers, and then selling it as one's own product shall be determined as infringing the trademark exclusive right of the original equipment manufacturer.

Plaintiff: Jiangsu Rugao Printing Machinery Factory. Domicile: Rucheng Town, Rugao City, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Sha Xiaoming, Factory Director of the said factory.

Defendant: Jiangsu Rugao Yide Materials Co., Ltd. Domicile: Rucheng Town, Rugao City, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Yao Zhenglan, Chairwoman of the said company.

The plaintiff, Jiangsu Rugao Printing Machinery Factory (hereinafter referred to as Printing Machinery Factory), believing that the defendant, Jiangsu Rugao Yide Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yide Company), had infringed its trademark exclusive right, filed a lawsuit with the Nantong Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province on June 10, 2003.

Plaintiff's Allegations: Since 2001, the defendant Yide Company has repeatedly purchased used offset printing machines bearing the "Yinzhi" (Silver Pheasant) trademark manufactured by our factory, refurbished them, and after removing our factory's "Yinzhi" trademark, sold them externally without any identifiers. This has hindered the expansion of the reputation of our factory's "Yinzhi" trademark, affected the market share of our offset printing machines, and constitutes infringement of our factory's exclusive right to use the "Yinzhi" trademark. We request a judgment ordering: (1) Yide Company to immediately cease the acts infringing the plaintiff's trademark right; (2) Yide Company to compensate the plaintiff for losses totaling RMB 50,000; (3) Yide Company to bear the plaintiff's attorney's fees of RMB 5,000 and investigation and evidence collection fees of RMB 10,000 incurred in this case; (4) Yide Company to bear the case acceptance fee and other litigation costs of this case.

Principal evidence submitted by the plaintiff:
1. A certificate from the Rugao Enterprise Reform Work Leading Group Office, the "Reply on Agreeing to the Transfer of Property Rights of Nantong Mining Machinery Factory Labor Service Company" from the Rugao Enterprise Reform Work Leading Group Office, and the business license of the legal person, to prove that Printing Machinery Factory is a legal person enterprise engaged in the manufacture and sale of printing machinery.
2. Trademark Registration Certificate No. 174737 issued by the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce, to prove that the registered trademark "Yinzhi" for printing machinery was acquired by Printing Machinery Factory through assignment from Nantong Mining Machinery Factory.
3. A video compact disc containing a recording of the infringing acts committed by Yide Company.
4. Three special value-added tax invoices to prove the price difference between the mechanical products of Printing Machinery Factory and the similar refurbished mechanical products sold by Yide Company.
5. Relevant receipts for attorney's fees and investigation and evidence collection fees paid by Printing Machinery Factory to stop the infringement.

Defendant's Defense: Our company, upon the entrustment of customers, repairs used offset printing machines produced by the plaintiff Printing Machinery Factory, and accordingly collects repair fees. There is no sales relationship between our company and the customers. Repairing used printing machinery for customers is a lawful act within our business scope, and does not infringe the trademark right of Printing Machinery Factory. Their claims should be dismissed.

The defendant Yide Company did not provide any evidence in its defense.

Upon the application of the plaintiff Printing Machinery Factory, the Nantong Intermediate People's Court conducted an on-site inspection and evidence preservation at the machinery manufacturing division of the defendant Yide Company, obtaining the following evidence:
1. At the production site of the defendant Yide Company, one aluminum nameplate bearing the "Yinzhi" trademark, the factory name of Rugao Printing Machinery Factory, product model J2101S(2), and the product name "Automatic Flatbed Offset Printing Machine" was found. There were several offset printing machines on site, and for the main component work numbers on one J2101S(2) Automatic Flatbed Offset Printing Machine, Printing Machinery Factory identified them as its own production work numbers.
2. One aluminum nameplate bearing the words "Manufactured by Rugao Biaochi Machinery Manufacturing Factory" and "YNAK Folio Single-Color Offset Printing Machine".
3. One aluminum nameplate bearing the words "Overhauled by Rugao Biaochi Machinery Manufacturing Factory" and "J2101S(2) Folio Single-Color Offset Printing Machine".
4. Eight contracts for the purchase and sale of industrial and mineral products with the defendant Yide Company as the seller.

Furthermore, upon the application of the plaintiff Printing Machinery Factory, the Nantong Intermediate People's Court also verified with the entities that purchased refurbished printing machinery from the defendant Yide Company. Printing Machinery Factory also dispatched technical personnel to identify whether the printing machinery purchased by the buyers were its own products. The result was: except for one printing device purchased by Zhenjiang Commercial Printing Co., Ltd., which bore the overhaul nameplate of Rugao Biaochi Machinery Manufacturing Factory, the other machinery had no nameplates or trademarks, making it difficult to identify the original manufacturers of these printing machines. The buyers only knew that the purchased printing machinery were second-hand equipment.

During the court investigation, the defendant Yide Company did not object to the fact that the "Yinzhi" trademark was acquired by the plaintiff Printing Machinery Factory through assignment. However, Yide Company argued that the product models recorded in the invoices for the sale of offset printing machines provided by Printing Machinery Factory did not match the models of the products repaired by Yide Company, and thus could not prove that Yide Company's acts caused economic losses to Printing Machinery Factory. Yide Company also argued that the plaintiff's evidence 3 was not reasonable.

Both parties did not raise any objections regarding the authenticity of the evidence preserved by the Nantong Intermediate People's Court. The plaintiff Printing Machinery Factory argued that the preserved evidence proved that the defendant Yide Company purchased used printing machinery manufactured by others, removed the original trademarks during repair, and then sold them as its own products. The defendant Yide Company argued that the preserved evidence only proved that its company engaged in the act of repairing machinery, and did not directly prove the infringing facts alleged by Printing Machinery Factory.

The Nantong Intermediate People's Court determined the facts of this case as follows:

The plaintiff Printing Machinery Factory is an enterprise engaged in the production and sale of printing machinery. After acquiring the "Yinzhi" trademark used for printing machinery from Nantong Mining Machinery Factory on December 20, 1991, it combined the trademark identifier, product technical parameters, and its own factory name to create product nameplates, which were affixed to the offset printing machines it produced. The defendant Yide Company was registered and established in July 1997, with its business scope covering the assembly, repair, and sale of printing machinery. Since 2001, the company has repeatedly purchased used "Yinzhi" brand printing machinery previously used by others, removed the machinery nameplates, repaired them, resprayed them, and sold them to users without any identifiers. Yide Company admitted to selling three printing machines through the above method, and the buyers of these three printing machines were unaware of the original manufacturer of the printing machines.

It was further ascertained that the plaintiff Printing Machinery Factory paid attorney's fees of RMB 5,000 and investigation and evidence collection fees of RMB 10,000 for this litigation.

The Nantong Intermediate People's Court held that the focus of the dispute in this case was: Whether the act of the defendant Yide Company in purchasing used "Yinzhi" brand printing machinery previously used by others, refurbishing them, removing the trademark identifiers, and then selling them to others, constituted infringement of the plaintiff Printing Machinery Factory's trademark exclusive right.

Article 3, paragraph 1 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China provides that the exclusive right to use a trademark enjoyed by the trademark registrant is protected by law. The plaintiff Printing Machinery Factory lawfully owns and has the right to use the "Yinzhi" trademark, and has the right to prohibit others from improperly using the trademark. A commodity trademark in a registered trademark, as a link between the trademark owner and the user of the goods, can only enhance the visibility and competitiveness of the goods when attached to the approved goods and circulated with them, enabling the user of the goods to recognize the producer of the goods and the full value of the goods, increasing the market transaction opportunities for the goods, and fulfilling the trademark owner's goal of achieving maximum economic benefits. Therefore, a commodity trademark and the goods have an inseparable attribute. The trademark owner has the right to demand the protection of the integrity of the commodity trademark at any stage of the circulation of the goods, to safeguard its economic interests. The act of removing the original trademark during the circulation of goods clearly severs the connection between the trademark owner and the user of the goods, not only depriving the user of the goods of the ability to know the actual producer of the goods, thereby depriving the public of the right to recognize the producer of the goods and the commodity trademark, but also terminating the market expansion attribute inherent in the goods, directly infringing the trademark exclusive right enjoyed by the trademark owner, and ultimately damaging the economic interests of the trademark owner. Therefore, the act of the defendant Yide Company in arbitrarily separating the "Yinzhi" trademark of Printing Machinery Factory from the goods bearing that trademark in a commodity transaction constitutes infringement of Printing Machinery Factory's trademark exclusive right.

The defendant Yide Company argued that it was merely repairing printing machinery for customers and did not infringe the plaintiff Printing Machinery Factory's trademark exclusive right. Repair is merely an act of providing labor and does not change the ownership of the subject matter. In this case, Yide Company first purchased used "Yinzhi" brand printing machines previously used by others, removed the nameplates bearing the "Yinzhi" trademark from the equipment, replaced damaged parts, resprayed them, and then sold them to users in its own name. This act is no longer a simple repair act, but rather a transaction of goods in which the refurbished "Yinzhi" brand used printing machines are sold externally as Yide Company's own products. Yide Company is not a qualified manufacturer of printing machinery equipment, and its approved business scope does not include the purchase and sale of used materials and equipment. By putting refurbished used "Yinzhi" brand printing machines on the market without a certificate of conformity, quality standards, or any identifiers, Yide Company not only violated the Product Quality Law and administrative regulations on industry and commerce, but more importantly infringed Printing Machinery Factory's exclusive right to use the "Yinzhi" trademark. Therefore, Yide Company shall bear the responsibility of ceasing the infringement and compensating for the corresponding losses. Yide Company's defense lacks factual and legal basis, and is not adopted.

Since both parties are within the same administrative region, the defendant Yide Company's sale of refurbished used printing machinery at low prices undoubtedly impacted the market for the use of printing machines. Therefore, it shall be determined that the plaintiff Printing Machinery Factory suffered certain economic losses as a result. However, as Printing Machinery Factory was unable to prove the losses it suffered, and Yide Company did not have normal financial records reflecting the profits it obtained from the infringement, the principle of statutory damages shall apply in this case. Additionally, the reasonable expenses incurred by Printing Machinery Factory to stop the infringing acts shall also be borne by Yide Company.

In conclusion, in accordance with paragraph (5) of Article 52 and paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 56 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China, the Nantong Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on October 24, 2003:

1. The defendant Yide Company shall immediately cease the acts infringing the plaintiff Printing Machinery Factory's exclusive right to use the registered trademark "Yinzhi" from the date this judgment takes legal effect.

2. The defendant Yide Company shall, within five days from the date this judgment takes legal effect, pay the plaintiff Printing Machinery Factory compensation for losses of RMB 40,000, and pay Printing Machinery Factory's reasonable expenses of RMB 12,000, totaling RMB 52,000.

After the judgment was pronounced, neither party appealed within the statutory period, and the judgment of first instance has taken legal effect.
